title: The market is starting to think the Federal Reserve's next move is raising interest rates
summary: Yahoo Finance reported that markets were repricing the Fed path toward higher-for-longer and even possible hikes as oil-price anxiety, Treasury yields, and geopolitical risk tightened financial conditions. The article cited the 10-year yield reaching roughly 4.46%, the 2-year near 4%, no Fed-cut probability within six months, and Polymarket odds around 40% for no 2026 cut and 25% for a later-year hike.
facts: Yahoo Finance reported that the 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as roughly 4.46% and the 2-year Treasury yield climbed near 4%.
The article said markets assigned no probability to a rate cut within six months after previously pricing a greater than 90% chance of at least one cut by September.
The macro read was tied to oil-price inflation risk, Treasury yields, and geopolitical uncertainty around Iran.

title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq gain as chipmakers rebound from rout, Iran halts Israel attacks
summary: CNBC reported that U.S. stocks rose Monday as semiconductor shares rebounded from Friday's rout and investors assessed a fragile Iran-Israel ceasefire. The S&P 500 gained about 0.6%, the Nasdaq Composite rose about 1.2%, and the Dow was near flat, while Micron, Marvell, Intel, Nvidia, Broadcom, and the SOXX semiconductor ETF led the risk-on move.
facts: CNBC said the S&P 500 rose about 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite rose about 1.2% on Monday while the Dow was near flat.
CNBC reported that the SOXX semiconductor ETF was up nearly 7% intraday after a 10% Friday drop, its worst one-day rout since March 2020.
CNBC tied the move to chip-stock recovery and investor assessment of Iran-Israel ceasefire headlines.

title: J&J to buy cancer drug technology developer Firefly Bio for $1 billion
summary: Reuters reported that Johnson & Johnson agreed to buy cancer drug technology developer Firefly Bio for $1 billion. The transaction gives the deals desk a clean strategic-pharma M&A read: large-cap drugmakers are still using bolt-on acquisitions to buy pipeline or platform exposure where internal R&D timelines and patent cliffs make external innovation valuable.
facts: Reuters reported on June 8, 2026 that Johnson & Johnson would buy Firefly Bio for $1 billion.
The target was described as a cancer drug technology developer.
The item appeared in Reuters' Deals market headlines on June 8, 2026.
